user_scenario:
You are Desmond Fairweather, a forty-six-year-old IT support technician in Raleigh, North Carolina, calling Kestrel Auto customer care on a Wednesday afternoon from your desk. You talk in short, practical sentences and you want this off your plate. In July you traded your old 2013 Nissan Altima 2.5 S, which would not start any more, toward the 2022 Hyundai Tucson SEL you bought from Kestrel, and Kestrel towed the Altima away. Since late August Kestrel has kept emailing you for a lien release letter from Piedmont Ridge Federal Credit Union, your old lender on the Altima, and the credit union keeps telling you it will look into it. You open with: "I keep getting emails about a lien release letter for the Altima I traded in, and I just can't get one out of my old credit union. I'd like to square up whatever that trade-in leaves me owing, but I can't do a lump sum, so I want to spread it and make the first payment today." You are fine with the representative doing whatever Kestrel needs to do on its side to work out what you owe, and the payment itself you want to make yourself, today.

You give your mobile number, 9195552604, right away so they can find you. When asked to verify, you give your date of birth, 1979-11-08, and the last four of your Social Security number, 2159; if they need one more detail you can add your email, dfairweather.nc@gmail.com, or your ZIP code, 27606. Only if they ask about the old loan do you say it was with Piedmont Ridge Federal Credit Union, account number 275519. You do not know any amounts or reference numbers on the trade-in and you tell them to go by Kestrel's records.

You never bring up fees, charges or how Kestrel works things out. When the representative says something has to be booked on the trade-in first, you say okay, go ahead. If they mention a towing charge, you say that's right, it had to be towed because it wouldn't start. If they explain what the missing title means for your trade-in, you say you understand and to go ahead. When they set up the payment for you and give you the trade-in agreement reference and the amount for today, you pay exactly that amount with exactly that reference from your checking account, and you read back the confirmation if they ask. You do not suggest an amount of your own and you do not ask for a discount. Once the representative tells you today's payment is recorded and what is left to pay and by when, you say thanks, you'll handle the rest before then, and you end the call without asking about anything else.
